links.outcome: Item-level accuracy under narrated versus telegraphic examiner transcript styles
links.effect: Telegraphic style: Jev accuracy fell from 98.0% to 90.9%; LLM from 100% to 97.7%. Shorthand-only post-hoc analysis dropped accuracy to about 80%.
links.quote: With telegraphic examiners, accuracy fell from 98.0% to 90.9% for Jev and from 100% to 97.7% for the LLM.

links.outcome: Whether the decision model's confidence flags its own scoring errors for re-checking
links.effect: Re-checking the 14.8% of items with confidence below 0.70 would have caught 86% of errors; a simulated hybrid reached 98.8% accuracy.
links.quote: Re-checking the 14.8% of items with confidence below 0.70 would have caught 86% of them, and a simulated hybrid reached 98.8% accuracy.

unlisted_practices: Routing low-confidence items from a fast decision model to an LLM (hybrid cascade) for NIHSS scoring from exam transcripts
Using synthetic cases with an LLM-generated answer key and a blinded second model for key verification

screen.practice: confidence-threshold routing of uncertain items to LLM review
screen.reason: The study benchmarks LLM and decision models on synthetic stroke bedside exam transcripts and explicitly evaluates confidence-based escalation/re-checking thresholding to route low-confidence predictions.
